notes.claim: If you know how the area of one unit square changes, you know how any region's area changes; the determinant is that scale factor.
A negative determinant means the move flips the orientation of space, and its size still gives the area scaling.
A determinant of zero means the move squashes all of space onto a line or a point, so every area becomes zero.
For a 2 by 2 matrix the determinant is the number ad − bc.

sources.title: The determinant | 3Blue1Brown
sources.quote: Any transformations that do this are said to "invert the orientation of space". Whenever this happens, the determinant will be negative.

sources.title: The determinant | 3Blue1Brown
sources.quote: if it squishes all of space onto a line, or even onto a single point, since the area of every region would then become 0.
